SAN FRANCISCO, October 13, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET), the leading connectivity cloud company, today announced that it will report its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 after the U.S. market closes on Thursday, November 5, 2026.

Cloudflare will host an investor conference call that day at 2:00 p.m. Pacific time (5:00 p.m. Eastern time) to discuss the results. Interested parties can access the call by dialing +1 (833) 461-5787 (North America) or +1 (585) 542-9983 (International) with conference ID 732669571.

A live webcast of the conference call will be accessible from the Cloudflare investor relations website at cloudflare.NET. A replay will be available approximately two hours after the conclusion of the live event and will remain available for approximately one year.

About Cloudflare

Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET) is the leading connectivity cloud company. It empowers organizations to make their employees, applications and networks faster and more secure everywhere, while reducing complexity and cost. Cloudflare's connectivity cloud delivers the most full-featured, unified platform of cloud-native products and developer tools, so any organization can gain the control they need to work, develop, and accelerate their business.

Powered by one of the world's largest and most interconnected networks, Cloudflare blocks billions of threats online for its customers every day. It is trusted by millions of organizations – from the largest brands to entrepreneurs and small businesses to nonprofits, humanitarian groups, and governments across the globe.

Learn more about Cloudflare's connectivity cloud at cloudflare.com/connectivity-cloud. Learn more about the latest Internet trends and insights at radar.cloudflare.com.

title: Does Zscaler Stock's Run Make Any Sense?
detail:
Does Zscaler Stock's Run Make Any Sense?
Trefis Team

FTNT
NET
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Zscaler (ZS) stock has climbed 56% over the past three months, comfortably outpacing the 2.8% gain for the S&P 500. Over twelve months, however, the stock is still down 26%. During this recent three-month stretch, the cybersecurity company posted 25% sales growth for fiscal Q4 2026 but projected slower growth for the year ahead. Management then reiterated that conservative outlook at an Investor Day on October 6, 2026. This presents a striking contradiction: investors are bidding up shares even as executives anticipate a slowdown. What could buyers be seeing that Zscaler's forecast does not spell out?

Zscaler Added New Subscriptions Faster In Fiscal Q4 2026

Zscaler measures its new business through the yearly subscription revenue it adds each quarter. Excluding the recent Red Canary acquisition, that revenue grew 17% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026. This represents a noticeable acceleration from the 10% growth recorded in the first half of the fiscal year, a detail management highlighted on a September 3, 2026 call.

Part of this momentum comes from the company's Security for AI products. Bookings for these offerings rose more than 50% from the prior quarter. Notably, Zscaler charges for almost all of these products based on usage.

Management added that its financial guidance does not specifically call out the contribution from Security for AI. Because buyers cannot see exactly how much of this contribution the forecast includes, they may expect these products to perform better than the official projections show.

What Are Buyers Of Zscaler Stock Paying For?

Investors are currently paying 11.3 times sales for Zscaler, compared with a multiple of 3.1 times for the S&P 500. Because the company lost money over the last twelve months, a price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful, and sales are the measure used here.

Zscaler differs from the broader index in how fast those sales grow. Over the past three years, Zscaler saw its revenue expand by 27.6% a year on average. During the same period, the S&P 500 averaged just 5.9% growth.

Moving forward, executives anticipate a slower year. They guided for fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 16.6% to 17.5%, a step down from the 25% growth achieved in fiscal 2026. Buyers appear willing to pay a higher multiple for growth, but Zscaler's upcoming results for fiscal 2027 will ultimately reveal how much of that growth remains intact.

Zscaler Has Just Changed Its Sales Leadership

Zscaler appointed a new chief revenue officer on September 24, 2026. On the September 3 call, management discussed a separate change: two regional and industry sales leaders had left, and that transition was built into guidance. The chief revenue officer change came three weeks later. Management repeated its guidance on October 6, after the appointment. Additionally, management expects the Red Canary acquisition to add no net new subscription revenue in fiscal 2027, because Zscaler is building that technology directly into its new Agentic SecOps product.

title: What Did Fastly Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
detail:
What Did Fastly Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
Trefis Team
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 4:20 PM MDT 4 min read
FSLY
^GSPC
NET
AKAM
ZS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Fastly (FSLY) stock returned 241.5% in the twelve months to October 9, 2026, easily outpacing the 17.0% gain for the S&P 500. Buyers appear to have been paying for a clear shift in the underlying business: sales began growing faster again, and losses shrank. Investors stepping in today are betting that this momentum will hold, while observers who missed the rally might wonder if the company offered advance warning. How early did Fastly show that its sales were turning?

Fastly Gave A First Sign In February 2025

The initial signal arrived on February 12, 2025, about eight months before the run began. During a quarterly earnings call, management outlined a new approach to how Fastly sells its products. The strategy involved pitching customers on the company's entire range, including security solutions and bot protection.

Management noted on that call that demand had weakened at a few of its largest customers. Revenue from clients outside its ten largest accounts, however, grew 16% year over year. Because total revenue grew only 2.0% in the fourth quarter of 2024, the health of those smaller accounts remained masked in the overall figures. Anyone buying the stock after that presentation was investing in a turnaround plan, not yet a proven result.

Fastly's Next Two Filings Backed The Plan

That strategy started taking shape across the subsequent two quarterly reports, both filed before the stock run. Fastly filed its results on May 7, 2025, showing revenue grew 8.2% in the quarter ended March 2025. Top-line growth then reached 12.3% in the second quarter of 2025, detailed in a report filed on August 6, 2025.

Some investors noticed the initial acceleration immediately. Fastly stock was up about 30% for the week by early Friday, according to a news report on May 9, 2025. The company's regulatory filings showed faster sales by August 6, 2025, two months before the twelve-month window that produced the 241.5% gain began.

Neither filing demonstrated a profit. Fastly's operating loss was still 24.6% of revenue in the second quarter of 2025. Anyone waiting for proof that revenue growth would translate into profit did not have it yet.

Are Fastly's Sales Still Picking Up?

Sales momentum continued through the latest reported quarter. Management announced on the August 5, 2026 call that revenue grew 23% to $183.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. Security revenue grew 43%, aligning with the strategy detailed in February 2025. The company's operating loss over the past twelve months narrowed to 12.0% of revenue, down from 24% a year earlier. Fastly's overall stock run was substantially larger than that of its peer Cloudflare, which returned 64.1% over the same twelve months.

Why Cloudflare (NET) Stock Is Up Today
What Happened?

Shares of cloud security and performance company Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) jumped 6% in the afternoon session after the company announced that the Deno team joined its platform to simplify self-hosting Workers and Durable Objects, while StreetInsider reported that Oppenheimer simultaneously raised its price target on the stock to $430 amid a broad tech sector recovery.

As detailed by Cloudflare in its corporate blog post, the technical combination involves merging workerd and celld to enable developers to seamlessly utilize identical primitives across multiple hosting environments. Separately, StreetInsider confirmed that Oppenheimer analyst Param Singh officially increased the firm's valuation estimate for the cybersecurity and infrastructure company. According to financial analysts, a price target directly represents a firm's formalized projection of a stock's future market value, with a higher target reflecting tangibly increased valuation expectations from institutional researchers.

Ultimately, the combination of expanding developer platform capabilities and bullish Wall Street sentiment provided a powerful catalyst for the stock, amplified by a highly supportive macroeconomic backdrop that gathered strength intraday. As reported by CNBC, major equity averages moved higher on Friday as dip-buyers quickly dismissed yesterday's OpenAI revenue concerns, viewing the private lab's shortfall as an attractive entry point rather than a structural risk to the enterprise software ecosystem.

The swift market recovery highlights enduring investor appetite for leading technology firms, even as Wall Street remains sensitive to updates on how quickly massive capital investments in artificial intelligence will translate into sustainable corporate profits.

Is now the time to buy Cloudflare? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What Is The Market Telling Us

Cloudflare's shares are extremely volatile and have had 38 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock gained 3.4% on the news that momentum from the company's product announcements carried into the session, amplified by corporate blog data ranking it as the fastest provider across 74% of the top 1,000 networks and a cooler-than-expected U.S. jobs report that sparked a broad rally in tech equities.
